open_points.subject: Owner, staff, and staff-credential principal
open_points.text: “Owner / staff” and “staff hold a staff credential”
open_points.question: Are the owner and all staff one undifferentiated security principal sharing a single credential, or are they distinct principals whose actions or credentials must be distinguishable?
options: One shared staff principal and credential
Separate owner and staff principals
Separate credential per staff member
open_points.default_guess: Treat owner and staff as one shared API principal because only one staff credential is specified.

open_points.subject: Staff credential holders
open_points.text: “staff hold a staff credential”; “the operator ... holds the staff credential”; “that server ... holds the staff credential”; “the configuration of the one holder it is for”
open_points.question: Is the staff credential intentionally shared by staff, the operator, and a frontend server, or must each credential have exactly one holder?
options: One shared staff credential with multiple holders
A separate staff credential for each holder
Only one designated holder, with the others acting through it
open_points.default_guess: Allow the same staff credential to be held by all named staff actors and treat “one holder” as applying only to service tokens.

open_points.subject: Operator authority
open_points.text: “It acts for the owner and holds the staff credential for every action it takes”
open_points.question: Does possession of the staff credential make the operator authorized for every staff action, including correcting and archiving projects and correcting or erasing customers, or only for the operator actions explicitly mentioned in the text?
options: All staff actions
Only create projects and rooms, publish artifacts, and read/list customers
A separately specified subset
open_points.default_guess: Authorize every staff action because Registry cannot distinguish holders of the same credential.

open_points.subject: Customer data in open project reads
open_points.text: “read a project context | any caller | ... address, customer” and “the customer's contact data ... readable by staff only”
open_points.question: What does the publicly readable `customer` value contain: only `customer_ref` and erasure state, or any Customer fields such as name, phone, e-mail, or language?
options: Only customer_ref
customer_ref plus erasure state
A customer summary containing selected contact fields
open_points.default_guess: Return only `customer_ref`, with no contact data.

open_points.subject: Host-only network enforcement
open_points.text: “The deployment enforces this; Registry itself does not tell callers apart by address.”
open_points.question: Which named deployment component or configuration action guarantees that Registry cannot be reached from another host, and what observable startup or health failure occurs when that guarantee is absent?
options: Registry binds only to an explicitly permitted interface
Container-network publication rules enforce it
A host firewall or reverse proxy enforces it
The deployment is not checked and correctness is purely operational
open_points.default_guess: Bind Registry only to loopback or a same-host container interface and fail startup for an explicitly external bind address.

open_points.subject: Configuration representation
open_points.text: “An instance's configuration is a file on its host” and “on a local instance the environment it is started with”
open_points.question: Is configuration always a file, or may process environment variables be the authoritative configuration source without a configuration file?
options: Always a file
File on VPS and process environment locally
Either file or process environment in every deployment
open_points.default_guess: Use process environment as the runtime interface, populated from a compose environment file on the VPS and directly in local runs.

open_points.subject: Invalid or incomplete configuration
open_points.text: “A change takes effect when the instance restarts”
open_points.question: What must Registry do at startup when required credentials, the frontend origin, or the artifact vocabulary are missing, malformed, duplicated, or mutually ambiguous?
options: Refuse to start with a configuration error
Start with invalid features disabled
Apply defaults where possible
open_points.default_guess: Refuse to start and identify the invalid configuration entry without revealing secret values.

open_points.subject: Cross-instance project-id meaning
open_points.text: “When two instances hold a project under the same id, they hold two independent records of one physical object.”
open_points.question: Who guarantees that the same caller-supplied id is not used for different physical objects in separate instances, and is identical id alone sufficient for consumers to treat records as referring to one object?
options: The caller guarantees the mapping
The owner guarantees the mapping operationally
Identical ids are only possible links and do not assert physical identity
Registry uses an external authority to verify the mapping
open_points.default_guess: Make the caller responsible and treat equal ids across instances as asserting the same physical object.

open_points.subject: Secret non-disclosure boundary
open_points.text: “never in a record, a log line or an answer”
open_points.question: Which components and logs are covered by this guarantee, including HTTP access logs, reverse proxies, frontend servers, operator output, and exception traces, and what must happen when a secret would otherwise be emitted?
options: Only Registry records, responses, and application logs
Every named holder and deployment component
A specifically enumerated set of components
open_points.default_guess: Apply mandatory redaction to Registry records, responses, application logs, and exception traces; treat logs of external holders as their own trust boundaries.
